newsitem.title: USA: Staples sees opportunities in FTC fight.
newsitem.headline: Staples sees opportunities in FTC fight.

text.p: Staples Inc's chief executive told reporters on Wednesday the Federal Trade Commission's actions blocking a merger of his company with Office Depot presented new opportunies.

Thomas Stemberg, chairman and chief executive of Staples, said the Massachusetts-based office-supply retailer expected 20 to 25 percent revenue growth through the end of the century, with or without the merger. He made his remarks after speaking to students at Babson College.
"One thing that's come out of this merger process is that we have been able, by studying the marketplace, to understand just how small a share of the market we actually posess," Stemberg said.

He said the 11-year-old company, which expects to have sales close to $5 billion in 1997, learned "how much business sits in America's drugstores. How much business Walmart is doing in our product categories."
"And therefore we see more opportunities to grow our business than we ever dreamed of before," he added.
A federal judge has set a May court date for Staples to argue that it should be allowed to go forward with its proposed merger of Office Depot.
Meanwhile, several states are considering taking action against the proposed merger of the two chains and say they need the secret information to decide whether to go ahead.
Their actions would be in addition to a Federal Trade Commission challenge. The FTC argues that the merger would raise prices to consumers.

Stemberg, along with Staples co-founder Leo Kah, were among four chief executives honored by the college as distinguished entrepreneurs. The others honored were Leslie Quick, Jr. chairman and CEO of the brokerage house of Quick & Reilly, and Willie Davis, a former Green Bay Packers football team and now head of All-Pro Broadcasting Company.
